corrected_draft.title: Trump Issues Executive Order on Agency Accountability
corrected_draft.description_short: On February 18, 2025, Trump signed Executive Order 14215, directing greater presidential supervision of executive departments and independent regulatory agencies.
corrected_draft.description_medium: On February 18, 2025, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14215, “Ensuring Accountability for All Agencies.” The order addresses presidential supervision of executive departments and independent regulatory agencies and directs agency officials to consult with the attorney general on legal interpretations. Its text does not terminate an independent-counsel statute or abolish special-counsel regulations. The federal independent-counsel statute had expired in 1999.
corrected_draft.description_long: On February 18, 2025, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14215, titled “Ensuring Accountability for All Agencies.” The order sets out a policy of presidential supervision over executive departments and agencies, including independent regulatory agencies, and directs agency heads to consult with the attorney general on legal interpretations. The event is an executive order about agency accountability and presidential oversight. Its text does not say that an independent-counsel statute is ended or that Department of Justice special-counsel regulations are abolished. The independent counsel provisions enacted in 1978 expired in 1999, so the claim that this 2025 order terminated that statute is also chronologically incorrect. It also required executive departments and independent agencies to submit significant proposed and final regulations to OIRA before Federal Register publication. OMB was directed to establish performance standards for independent-agency heads, while those agencies were to coordinate policy priorities with White House offices and appoint White House liaisons. The order’s text concerns executive-branch supervision and regulation review.
